### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via ref_id (literal, a string literal in SYS_FILE_REFERENCE_COLUMNS))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via installSysFileStorageOwnedColumnsGuard (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via ref_id (literal, a string literal in SYS_FILE_REFERENCE_COLUMNS), ref_object (literal, a string literal in SYS_FILE_REFERENCE_COLUMNS))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via released_ref_id (literal, a string literal in SYS_FILE_REFERENCE_COLUMNS), released_ref_object (literal, a string literal in SYS_FILE_REFERENCE_COLUMNS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `50d3373db0ad62dc1c0955ba81b17b346570079c` — the merge of head `7fc7033de3b8c45e516ba45ede12ee9928ebac7d` into base `776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 50d3373db0ad62dc1c0955ba81b17b346570079c && git checkout 50d3373db0ad62dc1c0955ba81b17b346570079c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610 7fc7033de3b8c45e516ba45ede12ee9928ebac7d && git checkout -B drift-repro 776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610 && git merge --no-ff 7fc7033de3b8c45e516ba45ede12ee9928ebac7d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 776c1d875b2d140b4c2419103a7ad8681c1d2610` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7fc7033de3b8c45e516ba45ede12ee9928ebac7d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-storage: `system-file.object.ts` (new `SYS_FILE_REFERENCE_COLUMNS` beside `SYS_FILE_STORAGE_OWNED_COLUMNS`; `readonly: true` on `ref_object`, `ref_id`, `ref_field`, `released_ref_object`, `released_ref_id`; the #27778 header statement on `key` / `status`), `sys-file-storage-owned-columns.ts` (`LIFECYCLE_OWNED_COLUMNS` = both lists; `dropStorageOwnedColumns` un-exported and renamed `dropLifecycleOwnedColumns`; one `warn` line), 8 new pins in `sys-file-storage-owned-columns.integration.test.ts`, the changeset (`@objectstack/service-storage` patch, ADR-0087 not-required). 4 files, +211/−9. Fixes #27767 + #27778 (ruling A 6545931776; triage 6510433159 step 2 / 6511387772; claim 6546009563; dev report 6546642607). Not governed.
Inputs: both cards' bodies, triage, seat-4 release 6539653511, ruling, claim and dev report, the PR body, the whole PR diff, `git grep` on `origin/main` (`dropStorageOwnedColumns` is referenced only inside its own file, so dropping the export breaks no importer; the five storage columns already carry `readonly: true` at the merge-base), check-runs (read 2026-10-31T17:53Z: all 48 latest-per-name check-runs completed, 33 success + 15 skipped, none failed, none running) — 48 checks. Nothing built or run here; the seat's numbers (24/24 targeted, 71 files / 1326 package, five ablations, 62 derived gates, dogfood 361 files) are the dev report's. The security-dispatch rule holds: this record stays at rule level, as the PR does.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Ruling A taken as written.** The five file-reference columns take the exact form #27765 gave the five storage-owned columns: `readonly` on the object (the engine's static readonly strip takes a non-system caller's value off an update, by id and by predicate, and lands the rest) and the same create-side guard dropping them from a non-system insert (row still written, still `pending`, one `warn`, no refusal). No new refusal code, no spec key, no governed path, no wiring change — the ruling's four "no"s all hold in the diff.
- **Form choice is sound.** A second named constant rather than one widened list keeps each owner's exact-five pin (pin 1 here, the #27765 pin for the storage set) and lets the guard read one concatenated list; the warn text now names both kinds of column. `installSysFileStorageOwnedColumnsGuard` keeps its name and the plugin wiring is untouched, so the #27765 pins and docs row 47g stay true.
- **The lifecycle still writes them.** Pin 6 drives claim, copy and release through a real `media.poster` field write and reads the five columns back; pin 7 shows a system create/update keeps its values; ablation A3 (claim without the system context, 8 red) shows the pins would notice a lifecycle writer that lost the system context.
- **Rider #27778.** Item 1: the header states the `key` / `status` presence invariant and that the declaration stays (triage 6511387772's choice, taken as written); pin 8 measures presign, complete and the field copy. Item 2: the export is trimmed and nothing imported it. Both ride without behaviour change.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — a non-system caller's value for five columns is no longer applied; correct and the arm the ruling named. `Metadata-protocol: none` — the ruling's own line; the `readonly` flag is a served-shape change of a system object's fields, which #27765 shipped under the same line, so the precedent holds. `patch` with ADR-0087 not-required: no key removed, renamed or re-shaped, no stored row rewritten. `Skills-docs: none` with the reason stated.
- **Left unedited on purpose, and rightly:** the pending #27399 changeset's "ownership" word (a rewrite is a release decision) and `system-context.mdx` row 47g (still true, incomplete) — both named in the PR; neither blocks.

### ② Rulings cited

- 6545931776 (director#2, Tesla 「同意」 batch #434 item 1, 2026-10-31T16:12Z): letter **A** — lifecycle-owned, `readonly` + the #27765 guard, system contexts maintain them, no new refusal. Implemented as ruled. No open ruling.

### ③ Narrowing / widening

- Narrowing: a non-system write (create, batch create, update by id, update by predicate) to any of the five reference columns is dropped; the rest of the write lands and nothing is refused. A caller passing `strictReadonlyWrites` on an update gets `ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED`, as for every readonly column today. Attaching a file to a record stays the file-field write.

### ④ Behaviour / flags

- Seat lands (Tier S path): draft → ready → queue after this record; the changeset ships `@objectstack/service-storage` patch.
- The contract-review-tier review the ruling required before the queue is this record.
